title: Impact release, interception and passage relay
summary: A small block (the cue) slides along a raised deck toward the robot side at the start. Strike it with the paddle so that it hits a spring-held gate latch and swings the gate open, releasing a ball (the payload) that waits behind the gate on an inclined chute; within 1 s of the cue's impact the ball must be past the gate and rolling down the chute. Intercept the ball with the paddle after it has left the chute, send it through a narrow passage between two walls, then touch it again and bring it to rest in a target zone on the table beyond the passage.
robot_setup: One Panda, base at (-0.45, 0, 0), yaw 0 (facing +x). Its hand carries a blue upright paddle: a box 12 mm thick (tool x) x 0.10 m wide (tool y, 2 x `tool_half`, `tool_half` = 0.05 m) x 50 mm tall (tool z), centred at the tool frame origin; its striking faces are normal to the tool x axis. The paddle hangs from a rigid side adapter (part of the tool): from the hand a horizontal bar at tool z = 0.035 runs from tool x = -0.12 to 0 at tool y = -0.13, then along y to y = -0.05, then a short post goes down onto the paddle's top edge at its -y end. The Panda TCP is at (-0.12, -0.13, 0.04) in the tool frame, so with the paddle upright the gripper points straight down, offset to the paddle's -y side. At the start the paddle is upright, rotated 0.35 rad (20.1 deg) about world z (tool x axis along (cos 0.35, sin 0.35, 0)), its centre at (0.236, 0.266, 0.197).
scene: A raised, low-friction blue deck runs along the world x axis on posts, with 4 mm high curbs along its -x end and its +y edge. An orange block, the cue (40 mm x 40 mm, 24 mm tall), slides along the deck toward -x from t = 0. Beside the deck an inclined grey chute (a trough 0.06 m wide with 12 mm side walls) runs downhill toward +x and ends above the table. An orange ball, the payload (radius 18 mm), lies on the chute held back by a gate. The gate is an amber plate on a vertical hinge whose blade lies across the chute (with a small darker block at the blade's tip); the same rigid piece continues past the hinge as a thin trigger tail reaching over the deck at the cue's height. A weak torsion spring holds the gate closed; pushing the tail toward -x or the blade toward +x turns the whole piece open about its hinge. On the table beyond the chute's low end two short orange walls (0.13 m long, 60 mm tall, 0.09 m apart inside) form a straight passage leading away toward -y and +x; the target zone is an unmarked spot on the table beyond the passage exit (see world goals). The table top is the world's z = 0 plane.
scene_privileged: Cue: box half-extents (0.02, 0.02, 0.012) m, mass 0.045 kg, friction 0.01, restitution 0.45. At t = 0 it is at (0.10 + `incoming_speed` x `preview`, 0.15 + dy, 0.1775) = (0.3275, 0.15 + dy, 0.1775) with velocity (-`incoming_speed`, 0, 0) = (-0.35, 0, 0) m/s (unimpeded it would reach x = 0.10 at t = `preview` = 0.65 s); dy ~ U(-0.006, 0.006) m drawn at reset (the only random draw). Deck ('cue_lane', static): slab top at z = 0.165 spanning x -0.33..0.45, y 0.02..0.21, friction 0.01; curbs 4 mm high: one 12 mm wide at the -x end (x -0.33..-0.318), one 6 mm wide along the +y edge (y 0.204..0.21), friction 0.3; two support posts. Chute ('payload_chute', static): floor top surface line from (-0.30, -0.06, 0.205) to (0.05, -0.06, 0.045), length 0.385 m, slope 24.6 deg, downhill unit vector (0.9095, 0, -0.4158), floor half-width 0.03 m, walls 8 mm thick and 0.012 m tall, friction 0.12. Latch: vertical hinge at (-0.185, 0, 0.17); blade 12 mm thick, 0.125 m long from the hinge toward -y, z 0.17..0.215; tip block 32 x 24 x 24 mm at the blade's end; trigger tail 6 mm thick, 0.13 m long from the hinge toward +y, z 0.171..0.195; density 220 kg/m^3, friction 0.2, restitution 0.35; hinge limits +-1.5 rad, joint friction `latch_friction` = 0.012, damping 0.001; torsion spring drive: stiffness `latch_spring` = 0.02 N m/rad, damping 0.001, torque limit 0.08 N m, equilibrium q = 0 (closed); a -x push on the tail or a +x push on the blade turns it toward positive q. Payload ball: radius `radius` = 0.018 m, mass `object_mass` = 0.035 kg, restitution 0.12, friction 0.2, at rest at reset at (-0.233, -0.06, 0.193), on the chute just uphill of the gate. Passage walls: two static boxes 0.02 x 0.13 x 0.06 m, yaw 0.583 rad, centred at (0.2749, -0.2475, 0.03) and (0.3667, -0.1870, 0.03); in passage coordinates (see world goals) they span along 0..0.13 m at across +-0.055 m (inner faces at +-0.045 m). Also announced at reset (fixed, not used by any predicate): `goal_target` = (-0.185, -0.06, 0.17), where the gate crosses the chute centreline. Paddle: `tool_mass` = 0.2 kg, `tool_friction` = 0.3, restitution 0.05. Table friction `table_friction` = 0.015.

phases.name: mechanical_unlatch
phases.text: the cue hits the latch (contact of the cue with the gate's moving piece: blade, tip block or tail) during this phase; call the time of the first such contact T. The gate counts as open once, after that impact, its angle about the hinge exceeds 0.45 rad (25.8 deg) in either direction while the ball's centre is more than 0.02 m past the hinge in +x. The phase completes when, after the gate has counted as open and no later than T + 1.0 s, the ball's centre is past the blade's tip at the gate's current angle q, i.e. more than 0.125 sin|q| + radius + 0.006 m (0.125 m is the blade length) beyond the hinge in +x, and the ball's velocity component along the chute's downhill direction is at least 0.4 m/s. If this has not happened by T + 1.0 s the task fails (payload_not_released).

phases.name: payload_interception
phases.text: the ball touches the chute at some point during this phase, and then the paddle touches the ball while the ball's centre is at world x > 0.10 m.

phases.name: passage_redirection
phases.text: the ball's centre is in the far part of the passage corridor: in passage coordinates across is within +-0.045 m and along is greater than 0.105 m, while the ball is not touching the paddle.

phases.name: payload_braking
phases.text: the paddle touches the ball at least once during this phase; afterwards the ball's centre is within 0.05 m (horizontal distance) of the zone centre, the ball moves at less than 0.035 m/s and touches the table, for 0.5 s without interruption. This completes the task.

task_failures: direct_latch_shortcut: at any time, the paddle touches the latch's moving piece (blade, tip block or trigger tail).

payload_not_released: during mechanical_unlatch, more than 1.0 s has passed since the cue first hit the latch and the release condition (gate open, ball past the blade tip, at least 0.4 m/s down the chute) has not been met.
contact_rules: Only the paddle (including its side adapter) may touch anything, and it may touch only the cue and the ball: touching the latch (which also fails the task as direct_latch_shortcut), the deck, the chute, the passage walls or the table is forbidden. No other part of the robot, the fingers included, may touch anything.
world_goals_fixed: Interception line: ball centre at world x > 0.10 m (payload_interception). Passage coordinates, horizontal: entry point E = (0.285, -0.163), travel direction u = (sin 0.583, -cos 0.583) = (0.5505, -0.8348), lateral direction w = (cos 0.583, sin 0.583) = (0.8348, 0.5505); along = (p_xy - E) . u, across = (p_xy - E) . w; the passage_redirection region is |across| < 0.045 m and along > 0.105 m. Zone centre Z = E + 0.215 u - 0.005 w = (0.3992, -0.3452) at z = 0.018, radius 0.05 m (horizontal), announced as `goal_zone`.
difficulty_note: The cue must be struck so that it hits the narrow trigger tail hard enough to open the spring-held gate promptly (the ball has to be on its way within 1 s), and the ball leaves the chute fast, so interception, redirection through a 0.09 m passage and braking to rest follow each other quickly.
standard_notes: The cue is already sliding along the deck toward the robot side at t = 0. The ball stays behind the closed gate until the gate is opened; once released it rolls quickly down the chute and off its low end.
